stem: Which young person best fits the SCHN Trapeze transition service?

options.text: A 17-year-old with a complex chronic illness currently treated at SCHN and an unclear health transition pathway
A 13-year-old with an acute injury needing short-term outpatient follow-up only
A 22-year-old already established with adult specialist care and a clear ongoing plan
A 27-year-old with chronic illness who has never been treated at SCHN
A 15-year-old with a brief self-limited illness and no chronic care needs

explanation: Trapeze is an SCHN transition service for young people with complex chronic illness who are currently treated at SCHN and have an unclear health transition pathway. A 17-year-old with those features best fits the service.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

optionExplanations.A: Correct because this young person matches the service profile: adolescent age, complex chronic illness, current SCHN care, and an unclear transition pathway.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because an acute injury with short-term follow-up does not represent complex chronic illness or transition care needs.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because this person already has a clear adult specialist plan, so they do not fit an unclear transition pathway.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because the service is for young people currently treated at SCHN, not someone who has never been managed there.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because a brief self-limited illness without ongoing chronic care needs does not require a transition service.
